chapter: Haiti, Artie Shaw and Los Angeles work
title: Unpleasant Dixieland jobs in San Diego
summary: Collins stopped taking pay gigs with Dixieland groups because the players were weak, not the style.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: But this is interesting how styles, you know, they -- it's just timeless, you know. That -- it proves that if you just stay on top of music, just stay and listen and you can -- your style stays young, you know. Of course now I have been thrown in with some Dixieland groups, some concerts here in San Diego. It's a Dixieland club there, and they always called me, and it's the most unpleasant thing in the world. I imagine -- well, I'll tell you what. It's not Dixieland per se, but it's the exponents of it, it's the players. They aren't very good players, and it's like a chore. As a matter of fact I finally started turning them down, I wouldn't even accept them.
But at first I thought it was the difference in

styles, but it's not, the difference in style. In retrospect it was just the guys you know, who -- they weren't the greatest players. And anyway, I stopped, I just stopped accepting jobs and it was a very good paying job. I could ill afford to do that but it was -- gosh, it was like I had been pulling teeth all, you know, playing this job.
